content:
SELECTED_INDEX: 3
CONFIDENCE: 0.33
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows 1) a strong carbonyl stretch at 1700 cm⁻¹, 2) two intense C–O-stretching bands at 1242 and 1033 cm⁻¹, 3) aliphatic-CH stretches at 2955–2990 cm⁻¹ and an aromatic-CH stretch at 3074 cm⁻¹, and 4) typical aromatic ring modes (1006 cm⁻¹ ring breathing, 1599 cm⁻¹ C=C).  
Only candidate 3 (COC(=O)c1ccccn1) contains an ester carbonyl (accounts for the 1700 cm⁻¹ band), a methoxy group (gives the strong 1242 cm⁻¹ νas(C–O), 1033 cm⁻¹ νs(C–O) and the CH₃ stretches at 2955/2988 cm⁻¹), and an aromatic heteroring to supply the 1599 and 1006 cm⁻¹ bands. The other carbonyl-bearing candidates lack methoxy CH₃ stretches or the pair of C–O bands, while candidates without a carbonyl cannot explain the intense 1700 cm⁻¹ peak. Hence candidate 3 fits the main Raman features best.
